content.thinking: I need to understand how notifications are created from events, how the activity service records changes, how organization owners are looked up, and how invoice numbers are generated. I also need to identify tests that might break when period behavior changes.
Every invoice must be published once as billing.
I need to review organization and subscription listings, including archived filters and owner IDs.

I need to understand how invoice numbers work.

Invoice numbers must be unique within the workspace. Periods advance by one interval from their end date. Monthly periods end on the same day of the next month, or the last day when that date does not exist. Annual periods end on the same day and month of the following year. A clamped day carries forward to the next period start.

The clamped day carries forward exactly one interval. A period ending on February 28 advances to March 28, not March 31. All date arithmetic will use UTC to avoid timezone issues.

Remaining time is rounded up to the next full day. Once a period ends, days left become zero.

Period length is at least one day and rounded to the nearest whole day. Proration divides the full period amount by the total days in the period and multiplies by days left, then rounds down. Adding seats during a period bills only for the remaining days.

Seat reductions or unchanged counts incur no charge. Free plans and trialing subscriptions are also excluded from invoicing.

When switching between paid plans, only a positive price difference per seat is billed for the remaining period. Downgrades and unchanged prices leave the period untouched.

Choosing a plan during an active trial costs nothing and preserves the trial period; the first invoice is generated when the trial expires.

The renewal job leaves trialing subscriptions untouched. This conflicts with the trial expiry job, which may be responsible for invoicing when a trial ends. I need to verify whether changing plans during a trial sets the status to active and triggers an invoice.

The current `updateSubscriptionPlan` forces status to "active" and leaves period dates unchanged. This would immediately trigger the renewal job to invoice when the trial ends. The new spec requires keeping the trial active and unchanged during a plan switch, so this behavior must be corrected.

The intended behavior for a plan change during an active trial is to leave the period dates unchanged and avoid charging immediately. The subscription should remain on its existing trial end date rather than starting a fresh paid period.

The subscription must become active when a plan is chosen during a trial. This ensures the renewal job invoices the subscription once the trial period ends. Leaving the status as trialing would cause the trial-expiry job to downgrade to free instead, which would prevent invoicing.

Leaving the free plan for a paid one starts a fresh period immediately and bills the full amount. Moving to the free plan charges nothing and leaves the existing period unchanged.

Changing only the billing interval on an active paid plan costs nothing and leaves the period unchanged. The interval field still updates for the next renewal. Seat changes during a trial or on a free plan incur no charge. Adding seats to an active paid subscription bills only for the remaining days. The specification does not address seat or plan changes while a subscription is canceled.

Only active paid subscriptions are charged. Canceled subscriptions remain active until their cancellation date, so the renewal job leaves them untouched. I still need to determine whether seat changes made while a subscription is canceled but before its cancellation date should incur any charge.

Canceled subscriptions are excluded from invoicing, so seat changes on a canceled subscription incur no charge. When a period has already ended, proration yields zero days left and no invoice is generated. Invoice numbers must be unique within the workspace; sequential numbering or timestamps could work, but the period itself should serve as the idempotency key to prevent duplicate invoices if the renewal job runs again.

Idempotency is achieved by persisting the new period end before the job finishes. A second run at the same instant then finds the period already advanced and does nothing.

If the job crashes after invoicing but before updating the period, a replay could duplicate the invoice. The fix is to check for an existing invoice tied to that period before inserting a new one.

A single period can carry multiple invoices, such as a prorated charge and a seat-add charge. The renewal job is idempotent because it advances the period end date; replaying after a partial failure then finds no work left.

The renewal job will advance the subscription period first, then insert the invoice, and finally emit the event. Before writing an invoice, it will check whether one already exists for that exact period start and amount to prevent duplicate charges if the job crashes after invoicing but before updating the period.

If the period advances before the invoice is written, a replay would see no work left and skip. The fix is to check for an existing invoice with the exact new period start and end before inserting, then advance the period if needed. The loop will run while the period end is at or before now.

I need to check the activity database schema for action enums and notification kinds used in more places.

Cancellation logic sets the plan to free and status to active. The cancelAt field becomes null, interval becomes monthly, and currentPeriodStart equals cancelAt with a one-month period end. A billing.plan_changed event fires from paid to free with a null actorId. An already-free canceled workspace is unlikely.

The billing loop processes workspaces in this order: skip archived and trialing or past_due statuses, then check canceled status. If cancelAt is null but the workspace is still marked canceled, the spec says to treat it as if the cancellation date has already passed.

A null cancelAt means the cancellation is not yet due. Active subscriptions with a cancelAt set should not occur in practice, so the status check alone is sufficient. Free plan renewals only shift periods and skip invoicing. Seat counts remain stable across consecutive periods processed in one run. Invoices are USD with no paidAt timestamp, and listInvoices already returns them ordered by periodStart descending.
Drizzle SQLite text enums are TypeScript-only. They do not enforce constraints at the database level.

The notification kind is TEXT without a check constraint.

I need to list all organizations and add `listLiveOrgIds` to the repository. I also need `updatePeriod` on the subscription repository.

When a user leaves the free plan, the period should start fresh at now with the chosen interval and invoice in full. The current `updateSubscriptionPlan` does not set the period, so I will handle that and invoicing in the service layer. When upgrading from free to paid, the period will be set during the same update. I will extend the repository with a more general update function. Trial periods will remain unchanged.

Status becomes active once the trial period ends. The first paid invoice is generated when that trial expires, and the trial itself is not invoiced.

If a user upgrades during an active trial, the status becomes active but the period stays locked to the trial window. The renewal job will invoice one new interval once the trial expires, and any elapsed trial time is not treated as paid.

If the trial already ended long ago, changing plans would leave the period in the past and could cause a catch-up job to over-invoice. The spec does not require special handling for this edge case, so it will be left as-is.

Leaving the free plan for paid starts a fresh period immediately and invoices it in full without proration. I will implement an `issueInvoice` helper used by both the renewal job and billing service. Invoice numbers will be sequential per organization, formatted as `INV-0001`, `INV-0002`, etc., derived from existing invoice counts.

Invoice collisions from concurrent runs are acceptable for this app. The renewal job will skip creating or emitting an invoice if one already exists for the exact same period start and end dates. Proration and renewal use different periods, so they do not conflict. If the job replays after an invoice is inserted but before the period is updated, it will find the existing invoice, skip insertion, and only update the period.

The renewal job runs in a strict order: compute the next period, insert and emit the invoice if none exists, then advance the subscription period. A crash after invoicing but before updating the period is safe because the replay will skip the duplicate invoice and only update the period. A crash after updating the period is also safe because no double invoice occurs.

After cancellation, the subscription becomes active free with no pending cancellation and a new monthly period starting at the cancellation date. If that period has already ended, the spec does not clarify whether to roll forward or issue a single free period.

If the cancellation date falls in the past, the job will roll forward through free periods without issuing invoices. The next run simply advances further into the free window. Replay is safe because once the period passes the current time, subsequent runs do nothing.

The renewal job will process cancellations and renewals in a single pass. After converting a canceled subscription to the free plan, the loop falls through to roll forward any free periods that have already expired.

I will persist the cancellation before emitting the plan change event to prevent duplicate notifications on replay. The organization plan column should also be updated to free, since the subscription is the source of truth.

The interval will be set to monthly when a subscription is canceled. Seat count remains unchanged. No invoice is generated on cancellation. The plan_changed event will have a null actorId. Invoice notifications will target only the organization owner. The notification service will register its fan-out handler.
